issues.title: [Revert] Revert "[Feature][Kernel] Extend split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope with value normalization for Gemma4" (#15332)
issues.body: Revert of PR #15332 (merged onto `main`). Original PR: #15332 Original author: @dwoai22 Merge commit: `166dcd38c6a78cb874850e03138462f564b437ea` --- ### What this PR does / why we need it? Gemma4 runs its pre-attention chain (qkv split, per-head q/k RMSNorm, RoPE, and a weight-less per-head **v** RMSNorm) as separate ops on Ascend. The existing fused `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` kernel cannot cover it because it copies V straight out of the fused QKV tensor, and the existing `qknorm_rope_fusion_pass` has no notion of the V norm. This PR adds a `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope_vnorm` Triton kernel and a graph fusion pattern that rewrites Gemma4's pre-attention chain into it. It replaces the `Gemma4Attention` monkey-patch used in the earlier revision of this PR, as requested in review. **Kernel.** A variant of `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` that normalizes V instead of copying it. Because V now needs the same float32 reduction scratch as Q and K, the separate wide-tile V loop that the base kernel uses for the plain copy no longer pays for itself, so V is folded into the q/k loop: - one `tl.load` covers the whole fused row (`total_hidden_size`) instead of two separate column segments; - one RMSNorm reduction covers every q, k **and** v head of the tile, reshaped to `(tile * (q_head_num + 2*kv_head_num), HEAD_DIM)`; - Q, K and V are then cut out with three `extract_slice` calls at head offsets `0`, `q_head_num` and `q_head_num + kv_head_num`. Q and K apply their weights and RoPE; V has neither, so it is a cast and a store that reuses the K output index and mask. This is valid because Gemma4's `v_norm` is the same per-head RMSNorm with the same `eps` and no learnable scale; only the weight application moves after the shared reduction. The kernel keeps everything else from `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope`: the 1-D grid over vector cores, the batched UB tiling, the per-tile cos/sin gather shared by all heads, and partial-RoPE support. The UB tiling factor grows by `4 * kv_hidden_size` to account for the V columns now living in the tile. **Fusion pass.** `QKVNormRopeFusionPattern` in `qknorm_rope_fusion_pass.py` matches the unfused chain (qkv split, per-head `npu_rms_norm` on q and k, `npu_rotary_embedding`, per-head `npu_rms_norm` on v) and replaces it with the new kernel. - **One pattern per attention shape.** Gemma4 alternates sliding layers (`head_dim` 256) and full attention layers (`head_dim` 512, fewer KV heads), and `register_replacement` bakes the split sizes and head counts into the traced pattern. The pass therefore registers the pattern once per distinct `(head_dim, num_heads, num_kv_heads)` among the model's attention layers, the same approach as vLLM's own `qk_norm_rope_fusion` pass. - **Dedup key.** `BasePattern` gains a `pattern_key()` method, which this pattern extends with its shape. Without it, the second shape's registration would be silently skipped. Existing patterns keep their keys unchanged. - **Rejecting other shapes.** The matcher treats split sizes as wildcards and rejects a graph of another shape by re-tracing the pattern against it. A size mismatch makes `split` raise `ValueError`, which the pattern converts to the `RuntimeError` the matcher treats as "no match", as vLLM's `qk_norm_rope_fusion` does. - The existing q/k-only patterns are unchanged and keep their `head_dim == 128` guard, so they cannot claim the q/k half of a Gemma4 layer and leave its v norm unfused. - The replacement applies no v weight. Every `v_norm` in upstream vLLM today is weight-less; a model with a learnable v norm would need the kernel extended first. **Proportional RoPE.** Full attention layers use `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding`, which implements proportional RoPE by zero-padding `inv_freq` and passing `rotary_dim=head_size` to the base class. Its cos/sin cache is therefore an ordinary full-width cache whose non-rotated pairs hold cos=1 and sin=0, and the kernel needs no layer-type knowledge. Upstream `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding` had no Ascend override, so these layers ran the PyTorch `rotate_half` implementation, which the pattern cannot match. This PR registers `AscendGemma4RotaryEmbedding`, which keeps Gemma4's cos/sin cache and runs the NPU rotary kernel (`npu_rotary_embedding`), as sliding layers already do. **When a layer fuses.** The pattern is registered when: - the model dtype is bfloat16 and Triton is available; - the hardware profile supports the new `HardwareCapability.GRAPH_QKV_NORM_ROPE_FUSION` (Atlas A2/A3). Ascend 950 routes `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` to a SIMT kernel and has no SIMT variant of this operator yet, so it keeps the unfused chain; - one token's tile fits a vector core's unified buffer. For gemma-4-31B, full attention layers need tensor parallel size 4 or more; below that they stay unfused and the pass logs it once. Layers that cannot match stay unfused without any check: KV-shared layers have no k/v norm, and a norm bias is applied as a separate add. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No API change. In graph mode (the default), Gemma4 on Atlas A2/A3 uses the fused pre-attention path automatically. The existing `fuse_qknorm_rope` option in `ascend_compilation_config` turns it off, together with the existing q/k fusion. With `enforce_eager`, no fusion pass runs and Gemma4 keeps the unfused chain. Full attention layers now run RoPE on the NPU rotary kernel instead of the PyTorch implementation, including when they stay unfused. ### How was this patch tested? Tested on 910B1, TP=4, dtype bfloat16 with gemma4-31b-it. **Performance** **Accuracy** | Benchmark | Unfused (baseline) | Fused (this PR) | |-----------|-------------------:|----------------:| | HumanEval | 96.74 | 96.74 | | GPQA | 76.09 | 76.28 | Averaged over 3 runs. **Correctness** pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.py - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607

issues.title: [BugFix][Ops] Fix racy RoPE position read in `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope`
issues.body:
### What this PR does
Fixes issue #16674 
`split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` produced wrong, run-to-run non-deterministic Q and K above a shape-dependent `num_tokens` threshold — `max|err|` up to **9.4** against the op's own `atol=5e-2`, failing on **6/6** consecutive calls with identical inputs. V was always correct.

### Root cause

The RoPE position was staged into UB as a tile, then read back one element at a time as a scalar:

```python
x = tl.load(positions_gm_ptr + pos_indices + pos_offset, mask=...)
...
pos = get_element(x, (i,))
```

`get_element` reads the scalar from the UB buffer that the same iteration's `tl.load` is still filling, with nothing ordering the MTE transfer first. From the second outer iteration onward the scalar unit can still observe the previous
iteration's position, so `cos`/`sin` are fetched for the wrong position and the whole row — every Q head and every K head — is rotated by the wrong angle. V skips RoPE, which is why only Q/K were affected.

Because `x` is reloaded once per outer iteration, the race requires `iter_num_per_vec > 1`. `batch_size_per_iter_per_vec` is sized from the UB budget, so a larger `q_hidden_size + kv_hidden_size` yields more iterations and failure at a smaller `num_tokens` — `(12, 1)` first fails at 1024, `(64, 4)` at 257. `num_tokens` 1 and 16 pass only because the single iteration reads a freshly-zeroed buffer.

### The fix

Read the position straight from global memory as a scalar. The UB round-trip, and with it the race, is gone.

```diff
-from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.triton_utils import extract_slice, get_element, get_vectorcore_num, insert_slice
+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.triton_utils import extract_slice, get_vectorcore_num, insert_slice
@@
-    pos_indices = input_batch_offset + tl.arange(0, batch_size_per_iter_per_vec)
     output_q_nblk_idx = tl.arange(0, q_hidden_size)
     output_q_nmask = output_q_nblk_idx < q_hidden_size
     output_kv_nblk_idx = tl.arange(0, kv_hidden_size)
     output_kv_nmask = output_kv_nblk_idx < kv_hidden_size
     sin_cos_range = tl.arange(0, ROPE_DIM)
     cos_sin_cache_offset = cos_sin_cache_gm_ptr + sin_cos_range
+    last_row = input_batch_offset_end - 1
 
     for iter in tl.range(iter_num_per_vec):
         pos_offset = iter * batch_size_per_iter_per_vec
-        x = tl.load(
-            positions_gm_ptr + pos_indices + pos_offset, mask=(pos_indices + pos_offset) < input_batch_offset_end
-        )
         mmask = (mblk_idx + pos_offset) < input_batch_offset_end
@@
         for i in tl.range(batch_size_per_iter_per_vec):
-            pos = get_element(x, (i,))
+            pos = tl.load(positions_gm_ptr + min(input_batch_offset + pos_offset + i, last_row))
             values_tmp3 = insert_slice(
```

Three hunks total; `get_element` becomes unused in this file and is dropped from the import.

**On the clamp.** `last_row = input_batch_offset_end - 1` is always `>= 0`: for a core with no work, `input_batch_offset_end == batch_size >= 1`. Rows past the end read the last valid position instead of going out of bounds, and their outputs are discarded by `mmask` further down. This preserves the previous behaviour,
where the masked `tl.load` yielded `0` and those rows harmlessly read `cos_sin_cache[0]`.

**Why not a vectorized gather.** Replacing the inner loop with `tl.load(cos_sin_cache_gm_ptr + x[:, None] * ROPE_DIM + sin_cos_range[None, :])` would also fix it and be tidier, but limited vector-indexed gather support on
this backend is the likely reason the scalar loop exists at all. This patch keeps the existing structure and changes only the racy read.

### Validation

Ascend NPU, bf16, `head_dim=128`, full RoPE. Shapes and tolerance are taken from the op's own nightly test (`NUM_QKV_HEADS`, `NUM_TOKENS`, `DEFAULT_ATOL = 5e-2`), plus `num_tokens=257` from the PR gate.

**1. Non-determinism is gone.** Bitwise comparison of 24 repeated calls with identical inputs:

| num_tokens | (12,1) before | (12,1) after | (64,4) before | (64,4) after |
|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 1 | stable | stable | stable | stable |
| 16 | stable | stable | stable | stable |
| 257 | stable | stable | **UNSTABLE** | stable |
| 1024 | **UNSTABLE** | stable | **UNSTABLE** | stable |
| 10240 | **UNSTABLE** | stable | **UNSTABLE** | stable |

**2. Results are correct, not merely stable.** Per-row comparison against a fp32 reference at `atol=5e-2`, plus a count of rows matching the *preceding* token's position (the original failure mode):

`(12, 1)`:

| num_tokens | before max\|err\| Q / K | after max\|err\| Q / K | off-by-one rows after |
|---:|---:|---:|:---:|
| 1 | 0.0119 / 0.0077 | 0.0119 / 0.0077 | 0 |
| 16 | 0.0156 / 0.0143 | 0.0156 / 0.0143 | 0 |
| 257 | 0.0300 / 0.0283 | 0.0300 / 0.0283 | 0 |
| 1024 | **7.8431 / 7.6423** | **0.0310 / 0.0309** | 0 |

`(64, 4)`:

| num_tokens | before max\|err\| Q / K | after max\|err\| Q / K | off-by-one rows after |
|---:|---:|---:|:---:|
| 1 | 0.0148 / 0.0077 | 0.0148 / 0.0077 | 0 |
| 16 | 0.0306 / 0.0146 | 0.0306 / 0.0146 | 0 |
| 257 | **8.0298 / 6.8400** | **0.0311 / 0.0156** | 0 |
| 1024 | **9.3595 / 6.4640** | **0.0293 / 0.0306** | 0 |

Two things to note: on shapes that already passed, before and after are **identical**, so the patch does not perturb correct results; and residual error on the fixed shapes is ordinary bf16 rounding, comfortably inside `atol=5e-2`.

**3. No performance regression.** Measured over 2 repeats × 300 iterations (200 warmup) per cell, all 8 shape/config cells came out at or below baseline. I am deliberately not quoting a speedup: in this eager micro-benchmark
`num_tokens=1` and `num_tokens=1024` both land around 47 us, so it is dominated by dispatch overhead rather than kernel time, and run-to-run spread (~10%) is comparable to the effect. The patch removes one UB transfer per outer iteration, so a regression would be surprising, but a proper device-side kernel-time measurement would be needed to quantify any gain.

### Also: schedule the test that would have caught this

`tests/e2e/nightly/.../triton/test_split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.py` already has a correct fp32 gold reference and covers the failing shapes. It has simply never been run — `git grep -c 'split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope' -- .github/` returns `0` on the
base branch.

Without this, the same class of bug regresses silently:

```diff
       - name: rejection-sample
         os: linux-aarch64-a2b3-1
         tests: tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_rejection_sample.py
+      - name: split-qkv-rmsnorm-rope
+        os: linux-aarch64-a2b3-1
+        tests: tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.py
```

Per the header comment in `nightly_config.yaml`, this can be exercised on this PR without merging via `/nightly split-qkv-rmsnorm-rope`. Happy to add the matching `a3:` entry, or to split the CI change into a separate PR if preferred.

Separately, the PR gate `test_graphex_qknorm_rope_fusion.py` runs at `num_tokens=257` — a failing shape for `(64, 4)` — but only asserts `expect_fused=True`. Adding a numeric assertion there would turn it into a real guard. Left out of this PR to keep the change focused.

issues.title: [Doc][Ops] Add standard, multimodal, and TP QKV RMSNorm RoPE operator descriptions
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds three related Triton operator documents under
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/`:

- `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.md` documents the fused QKV split, Q/K RMSNorm,
  optional bias, and NeoX-style RoPE operator;
- `split_qkv_rmsnorm_mrope.md` documents the multimodal RoPE variant, including
  the optional attention-gate extraction and interleaved MRoPE layout;
- `split_qkv_tp_rmsnorm_rope.md` documents the two-stage Tensor Parallel
  pipeline formed by `_split_qkv_and_compute_local_qk_var_kernel`, the TP
  all-reduce, and `_apply_global_rmsnorm_kernel`.

The documents describe the formulas, fused execution flows, parameter layouts,
hardware routing, constraints, production call paths, and existing accuracy
test coverage.

They also record the current test-coverage boundaries: the MRoPE optional-bias
branch is not covered, and the TP test executes both kernels with `tp_world=1`
but does not exercise a multi-rank all-reduce.

Documentation only; no operator source or test file is modified.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This PR only adds documentation for internal Triton operators and does not
change any API, interface, numerical result, or runtime behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

The repository pre-commit workflow was run in the `zrr_dev` Linux container on
the exact PR commit, and all hooks passed:

```bash
bash format.sh ci
```

A non-empty Gitleaks scan of the PR commit range also reported no leaks.

The documents reference the existing accuracy tests below. The tests themselves
are not modified, and no NPU test was rerun for this documentation-only patch:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.py
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_split_qkv_rmsnorm_mrope.py
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_split_qkv_tp_rmsnorm_rope.py
```

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba07e4a48fc951300d97eb506217dd530583dea3
